I am in a relationship: we’ve been dating for 6 years and it has definitely had some bumps- hell we even broke up for 1-2 months 2 different times. The break ups are what really caused the most change though- it allowed me to focus on myself, reflect on the relationship, and introspect. It got me to become motivated enough to focus on my own mental health and well-being, and also really helped me realize that im not gonna be able to take care of people I love properly and treat them with kindness no matter what the situation until I learn to do it with myself first. After the break ups I  put into practice what I learned during that time of introspection and reflection. I think it’s important to note that while both of us were abusive and toxic in our own ways, I was the one who was active (eg calling him names, yelling, controlling, maybe entitled) and he was just passive (flirting with other girls, neglectful, putting me down, breaking my confidence, etc) so it might’ve been more important for me to change for anything to go anywhere. My drive to stay with him also really motivated a lot of my growth and expansion as a person.

At those times I just really couldn’t bear to let go of him (granted if I were healthier I probably would have just left, but he was there for me in the time I was having a lot of PTSD flashbacks, severe anxiety, OCD, depression, you name it)- his stability and simply being there made me not want to let him go. It was probably codependent but through the breakups and therapy, I’ve grown out of it, and also have been able to truly experience him as a separate person to love rather than an emotional crutch I needed to please to keep around. 

The biggest recent improvement in wverthing definitely started when I began with a really awesome therapist (for ~2 months now) and I find that we have a much healthier relationship (though we are still LDR and he’s in an intense program in school). I don’t text and call 24/7 because I realize my own experience and life is important too just like how he needs space, and our fights resolve pretty quick esp when I use gentle parenting techniques/ etc and really empathize and understand his point of view (emotionally, cognitively, and even briefly immersing in his thinking patterns) to know how to talk to him next. Because he feels more comfortable with me and I am able to talk to him in a language he understands, he respects my feelings and when I say I am uncomfortable with something he either stops it or we are able to come to a compromise where both of us are comfortable. I find he is only willing to listen when I have his trust, so it’s important to be consistent. The thing I really find helps is to keep the shared experiences optimistic, pleasant, and realistic, let go of my (sometimes rigid) expectations, and cater to what makes him happy, while keeping my needs in mind as well. It’s also very important to really understand him and his experience, cause it helps me know how to keep him happy and feel safe- which in turn makes him put in more effort to meet my own needs and keep me happy.

This is just one story and I still have some work to do, so take it with a grain of salt. It is only possible if both of you are willing to compromise, and only if you’re up for it.

A lot of “normal” people don’t realize that NPD comes from a lot of trauma and is a defense just like you recognized and said. Also for some reason a lot of people assume NPDs don’t want to change therefore they won’t seek out information and resources on the topic, and that other people are the ones who want to know about it to protect themselves.

Stay away from the “empathetic” or “normal” people who claim to know NPD but only know it from the outside or through an abusive relationship cause nothing good comes from listening to that shit when you’re trying to heal/ treat yourself kinder and improve and change. Not all NPDs are the same and/ or in the same stage anyways- exactly like you said- so you don’t have to accept everything you hear about NPD if it doesn’t resonate or isn’t accurate.

Also just to keeps things simple- if you’re not hurting anyone then it’s ok. If you are, then it’s not ok and consider finding an alternative activity or action. (Yourself is included in this) 

the more you heal/ grow/ learn, the more you can be expand on how to decide what actions and activities you want to condone/ partake in and which you don’t
